summary: Research instructions now assess factual verification separately from audience beliefs, faction credibility and perceived personnel competence. A disputed allegation can expose a supported political vulnerability without establishing misconduct or representative persuasion.
scope: Prospective process correction across shared analysis, research priorities, maintained assessments, daily nominee monitoring, weekly projection and support-base research.
changes: Added separate judgments for underlying conduct, exposure, observed reception, inferred present vulnerability and projected behavior.
Required consequential reception and counter-move searches, with original-episode versus excerpt/reporting coverage explicit.
Added responsibility tracing through officials, factions and the appointing leader, plus common-standard personnel competence comparisons.
Required supported political implications in maintained summaries; score or daily odds holds explain their dimension or cadence.
Updated prompt metadata, research-workflow documentation and impersonal project memory.
limitations: This is a process correction, not a new political intake or claim about audience agreement.
The completed daily research and forecast history remain unchanged; no nominees, numerical formula, scenario inputs or odds were changed.
Existing record fields carry the analysis; no new mandatory schema or automatic reputation score was added.
Future reviews must obtain reception evidence and qualify the breadth of inferred effects.
validation_results: PASS: database validation (13 collections, 650 events, eight nominees); two existing database/prompt-composition tests; git diff --check. No application code or forecast inputs changed.
